name.en: the coupling of d into c acts at each step

statement.en: at every step some formation present outside the part exchanges with c, with positive strength k, on the level of d at that step: it couples d into c (∀ t, ∃ h, h ∈ present t ∧ part h = false ∧ 0 < k t h c t d); c and d are one condition for a coupling into itself

corrections.why: The statement reverses the coupling. In Frequency.lean k t h c s d is the strength with which h exchanges with c on the level of d at step s (CouplesAt, Remainder.lean:262; strengths and ZeroFrom, Frequency.lean:1122, 1131, read it as 'd into c'), and the laws stops_iff and floored conclude about the coupling of d into c (StopsBy ... d c, CouplingRecurs ... d c). 'couples c into d' says the opposite direction.

statement.en: at every step, while less than A has passed, some formation present outside the part exchanges with c, with positive strength, on the level of d at that step: it couples d into c (∀ t a, a < A → ∃ h, h ∈ present t ∧ part h = false ∧ 0 < sat a t h c t d)

corrections.why: Same reversal as saturation-acts: sat a t h c t d is a strength of d into c (stops_by's docstring, Frequency.lean:1283: 'some formation present outside the part reads the level of d at each step'; its conclusion is StopsBy ... d c A).
